set.st: A Barron County farmer, on the place since about 1897, hid his savings in sacks and in the ground. After his wife died in July 1925 about $6,000 was recovered: a flour sack, a poppy-seed sack, some buried, and more than $1,000 in an old coat ruined by mice. He said "there is a large quantity of silver buried between the road and the house." No later dig or find was reported 1925-35. The pin is the Vejvoda strip on the 1914 and c.1918 plats. Since his wife died in July 1925 he had been digging up money she hid in various spots on the farm; about $6,000 was found, and he was still looking for more. John and his wife came from Bohemia about 1895 and bought the farm about 1897; she "acted as banker and buried and hid the money." After her death he held a public sale.
